added_models.model: Dog cardiovascular telemetry (QTc) with hERG assays

safety.confidence_note: Year is a proxy: the palbociclib dog telemetry study (13GR248) is undated in the review; 2004 is palbociclib's first-in-human year.
safety.note: Telemetered beagles given palbociclib showed small concentration-related QTc increases above clinical exposure.
safety.short: Dog telemetry flags small QTc rise
safety.quote: Oral administration of PD-0332991 at ≥3 mg/kg resulted in increases in the QTc-interval that correlated with individual animal PD-0332991 plasma concentrations.
safety.judgement: Separate system from the repeat-dose rat/dog toxicology track: single-dose safety-pharmacology telemetry plus in-vitro hERG.

safety.magnitude_basis: dog QTc up to 9 ms at ~4x clinical unbound Cmax vs no QTc change >20 ms (slight positive slope) in 184 patients
safety.population: Advanced cancer patients on palbociclib 125 mg
safety.confidence_note: Both sides from the 2015 FDA palbociclib reviews; the reviews do not set them side by side, so this is a pairing.
safety.note: Patients showed no clinically relevant QT prolongation at 125 mg, as the dogs' small effect at fourfold exposure implied.
safety.short: Palbociclib: no clinical QT signal, as predicted
safety.quote: Palbociclib administered to steady state does not prolong the QT interval to any clinically relevant extent.
safety.judgement: Dog effect (up to 9 ms QTc) appeared only at about 4x clinical exposure; a clinically negligible effect at 1x is agreement, not a missed harm.

safety.magnitude_basis: dog AUC at QTc onset (21125 ng*h/mL) vs patient AUCss at 600 mg (23800 ng*h/mL)
safety.population: HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer (ribociclib 600 mg)
safety.confidence_note: Quote verbatim in the bundled 209092 Multidiscipline review text.
safety.note: FDA: ribociclib prolonged QTc in dogs at patient-level exposure, matching the QTc prolongation seen in trials and labelled.
safety.short: Ribociclib QTc predicted at clinical exposure
safety.reason: FDA states dog QTc matched clinic
safety.quote: caused a dose-related prolongation of QTc interval in dogs at an exposure similar to patients receiving the recommended dose of 600 mg, consistent with QTc prolongation observed clinically.
safety.judgement: Stated comparison by FDA; the dog exposure at QTc onset was within 2x of patient steady state, so the margin was placed correctly.

added_models.model: Human bone marrow mononuclear cells in vitro

safety.magnitude_basis: marrow suppression at clinically relevant concentrations vs dose-limiting neutropenia in patients
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (paywalled, not in PMC). Patient neutropenia as the DLT was public from Flaherty 2012 (doi:10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-11-0509).
safety.note: Human marrow cells reproduced palbociclib's reversible, non-apoptotic marrow suppression after neutropenia was known as its dose-limiting toxicity.
safety.short: Human marrow cells reproduce reversible neutropenia
safety.quote: This work demonstrated that palbociclib-induced bone marrow suppression occurred through cell-cycle arrest, with no apoptosis at clinically relevant concentrations, was not lineage-specific, and was reversible upon palbociclib withdrawal.
safety.judgement: Retrodiction: the assay was built to explain neutropenia already seen in patients (Phase 1 2011, label 2015), so retro, not same.

added_models.model: Rodent brain penetration and intracranial xenograft (abemaciclib)

dose.population: HR-positive breast cancer with brain metastases
dose.note: Mice and rats: abemaciclib reached unbound brain levels above CDK4/6 Ki, about tenfold more efficiently than palbociclib.
dose.short: Rodents predict CNS exposure above Ki
dose.quote: These data show that abemaciclib crosses the blood-brain barrier and confirm that both CDK4 and CDK6 inhibitors reach unbound brain levels in rodents that are expected to produce enzyme inhibition

dose.population: HR-positive breast cancer with brain metastases
dose.magnitude_basis: unbound brain-metastasis abemaciclib 96x (CDK4) / 19x (CDK6) above IC50, yet iORR 5.2%
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; dated to the NCT02308020 registry results posting (2019-12-19), before the 2020 paper.
dose.note: Brain-metastasis tissue exposure far exceeded target, as rodents predicted, but intracranial response missed its primary endpoint.
dose.quote: Abemaciclib achieved therapeutic concentrations in brain metastases tissue, far exceeding those necessary for CDK4 and CDK6 inhibition.
dose.judgement: Exposure target was met in human tissue; under the dose table a reached-but-failed, unpursued indication is contra derived from efficacy, so the failure is counted with efficacy.

efficacy.population: HR-positive breast cancer with brain metastases
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. The intracranial efficacy model was U87MG glioblastoma in rats, not breast cancer; the paper frames it for brain metastases too.
efficacy.note: Abemaciclib prolonged survival of rats with intracranial U87MG tumours, with brain exposure above CDK4/6 Ki.
efficacy.quote: Orally dosed abemaciclib significantly increased survival in a rat orthotopic U87MG xenograft model compared with vehicle-treated animals

efficacy.population: HR-positive breast cancer with brain metastases
efficacy.magnitude_basis: intracranial ORR 5.2% (cohort A, HR+/HER2-) vs predicted intracranial activity
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Pairing of a glioma model with a breast brain-metastasis trial; iCBR was 24%, so a cytostatic signal may exist below the iORR bar.
efficacy.note: In HR+/HER2- brain metastases, abemaciclib gave an intracranial response rate of 5.2%; the study missed its primary endpoint.
efficacy.quote: This study did not meet its primary endpoint.

patient_trials.quote: This study did not meet its primary endpoint.

efficacy.judgement: Scored on the primary endpoint (iORR); the rodent prediction was about CNS antitumour activity, which response did not show.

considered_not_added: PALLAS / PENELOPE-B adjuvant failures: patient results for the existing cell-line track, not a new model system; belongs in the main draft's efficacy cell (checker's rule question).
Cell-line RB1 loss / p16 / cyclin D1 biomarker predictions vs PALOMA ctDNA and biomarker analyses: same system as the draft's breast-cell-line-panel track (already scored partial in PALOMA-1).
Patient-derived organoids (Lin 2024 Int J Cancer, doi:10.1002/ijc.34945): 78.4% accuracy pooled across drugs; abstract gives no palbociclib-specific organoid-vs-patient concordance.
Breast PDX panels (e.g. NPJ Breast Cancer 2025 PDX screen): preclinical combination screens, no co-clinical comparison with patient outcomes found.
Trilaciclib mouse marrow myelopreservation: compared with patients in SCLC and TNBC, outside the HR+/HER2- population.
QSP / semi-mechanistic neutropenia models: those found are fitted to patient data (popPK/PD), not preclinical predictions; none chose a dose prospectively from preclinical data.
Abemaciclib dog telemetry: the 208716 review grep found no QTc finding, so the dog-cv-telemetry track carries only palbociclib and ribociclib.
Dalpiciclib, lerociclib: xenograft efficacy only, same system as the draft's tracks; no separate patient comparison found.

gaps.lead: Efficacy: PALLAS (palbociclib adjuvant, failed iDFS; Mayer 2021 Lancet Oncol, PMID 33460574)
gaps.detail: Patient result for the existing breast-cell-line-panel efficacy track (entries untested/same via PALOMA-1), not a new system; whether it is a 2020-21 contra or an untested condition is the checker's open rule question on adjuvant settings.

gaps.lead: Efficacy: PENELOPE-B (palbociclib post-neoadjuvant, negative iDFS; Loibl 2021 JCO, PMID 33793299)
gaps.detail: Same as PALLAS: a candidate status entry on breast-cell-line-panel efficacy, pending the checker's adjuvant rule question; no new model system.

gaps.lead: Safety: ribociclib dog telemetry QTc consistent with clinical QTc prolongation (FDA 209092 Multidiscipline review 2017)
gaps.detail: dog-cv-telemetry, safety cell, 2017 'same' entry (comparison_stated true, FDA 209092 quote); checker confirmed it (safety index 6).
